When I got back to school, I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eShop. So, I just deleted his profile. Now, this early morning, I got on the train to go to my dad's for Thanksgiving. I usually go home to my mom's, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family, and I'm not up for going on a plane trip. Anyway, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago, my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying. Not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my Switch over when I visit. So, was it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me think about this step by step. First, I made the profile for him to use while I was watching him, so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seems reasonable because I wanted to protect my own games and progress. But then, when I got back to school, I got annoyed with having to switch profiles each time I used the Switch. So, I deleted his profile to make it easier for myself. But now, when I brought the Switch over for Thanksgiving, my stepbrother wanted to play, and when he found out his profile was deleted, he got upset. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I knew he was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. But in this case, I did bring it, and my stepbrother wanted to play. So, by deleting his profile, I took away something he was looking forward to and enjoying. Maybe I should have considered how important that profile was to him before deleting it. Even though it was my Switch, and I have the right to manage the profiles on it, deleting someone else's profile without discussing it first could be seen as mean or unfair. I should have talked to him about it or found another way to manage the profiles without deleting his. Maybe I could have just logged out or set up a different system to keep my saves separate without deleting his profile entirely. In the end, my stepbrother was upset, and my dad thinks it was mean. So, even though I didn't think it was a big deal, it affected him negatively. That makes me realize that my actions had consequences for someone else, and I should have been more considerate. So, in conclusion, deleting his profile without discussing it first was probably not the best decision. It might have been more considerate to talk to him about it or find another solution to manage the profiles on the Switch.
